title.narrative: AGRICULTURAL SERVICES AND PRODUCER ORGANIZATIONS PROJECT

description.narrative: The proposed the project will be the first phase of the long-term Program (11 years). The project would support the Government of Benin to develop and widely share agricultural growth. In this regard, the project will (a) increase agricultural productivity through improved research and extension and adequate access to necessary inputs, (b) diversify export market opportunities, add value to agricultural products and develop agro-processing, (c) improve rural infrastructure, consolidate and expand the mobilization of financial resources and credit activities, (d) provide training, communication means, technical and organizational support to Agricultural Producer Organizations (APO) in order to assist them in providing services to their members and strengthen their capabilities to organize, manage, negotiate and have financial means to : (i) provide services to producers, help them access inputs, credit or marketing; (ii) participate in adaptive research; (iii) disseminate information on technologies on production and marketing; and (iv) be effective partners in the agricultural technology and transfer system through their capacity to diagnose, aggregate, prioritize, and articulate their members needs and constraints. The project will support three key activities: a) strengthening of the capacity of the Ministry of Rural Development (MDR) at national and central level; b) support to agricultural producer organizations; and c) support to agricultural research and extension and soil fertility.

title.narrative: Building a Results-Based M&E System for a Decentralized MAEP Administration

description.narrative: Summary of proposed activities to be funded by the IDF Grant 1a. Assessing MAEP needs and readiness to M&E This component includes a review of MAEP's current capacity to monitor and evaluated, and will help identify any gaps in capacity needed to build and sustain a results-based M&E system. 1b. Building the capacity of the M&E Leadership Team and the DPP The purpose of this component is to conduct a series of workshops which will help to achieve this goal. It will focus on knowledge sharing wiht international practitioners, as well as on case studies. 1c. Developing a results-based M&E toolkit The purpose of this component is to develop a toolkit which will provide the knowledge base and guidance to the actors that will be implementing the M&E system. 2a. Selecting the key parameters for a results-based M&E system in MAEP This component consists of a number of guided consultations with the Leadership Team to finalize the key building blocks of the M&E system. 2b-2c. Applying MAEP's newly developed results-based M&E system This component involves integrating the theorical framework developed under 2a. in a computer-based environment in order to facilitate the continuous process of M&E and to operationalize the corresponding management information system. 3a-3c. Sustaining and scaling-up MAEP's results-based M&E system This component will ensure that the results-based M&E developed in maintained and implemented beyond the lifetime of the project. The purpose of the grant is to strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Agriculture Livestock and Fisheries (MAEP) to develop and apply a results-based monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system, in order to:(i) help strengthen MAEP's institutional performance in the context of a decentralized administration; and (ii) increase the contribution of the agricultural sector to the achievements of the PRSP objectives.

The proposed IDF Grant is to support the strategy of the Beninese government to combat financial crime and more specifically money laundering and terrorist financing, by helping institutions with a stake in the fight against those two forms of crimes to build up management and operational capacity and effectiveness on anti-money laundering and combating financing of terrorism (AML/CFT). The components of the grant are expected to play an important role in spearheading this objective by helping the Beninese authorities to: (i) reinforce the operational capacities of the Cellule Nationale des Information Financiè res (CENTIF), the Financial Intelligence Unit responsible for receiving, analyzing and processing suspicious transaction reports; (ii) enhance compliance with AML/CFT legal obligations; and (iii) strengthening the law enforcement response to AML/CFT. The objective of the project is to improve the reporting, analysis, and investigation of suspicious transaction reports (STRs) by the private sector and key Government agencies involved in anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing (AML/CFT) in Benin, including the judiciary. This will be achieved by: - reinforcing the operational capacities of the financial intelligence unit (FIU), the Cellule Nationale pour le Traitement des Informations Financières (CENTIF) to analyze suspicious transaction reports (STRs) filed by the private sector; - improving the reporting of STRs by the private sector and - ensuring an adequate handling of money laundering and financial crime cases by the judiciary.

title.narrative: Institutional Strengthening of the Ministry of Development

description.narrative: This proposal is a response to the official request made to the World Bank by Benin's Ministry of State in charge of Planning, Development, Assessment of Public Policies and Coordination of Government Action (Ministère d'Etat chargé de la Prospective, du Développement, de l'Evaluation des Politiques Publiques et de la Coordination de l'Action Gouvernement - MPDEPP-CAG) for the strengthening of its institutional capacity. This ministry plays not only the traditional role of a Planning Ministry, but also the critical role of Government Coordination, which is usually devoted to a Prime Minister's office. Benin's ambition to become an emerging economy by 2025 can only be achieved with excellent performance of its public administration. This is not the case yet as there are significant shortcomings in the public administration in terms of institutional, organizational, and individual capacities. MPDEPP-CAG wants to play the leading role for building of an effective administration. Government's strategy is to strengthen this top ministry so as to create multiplier effects to the rest of the administration. In the orientation note prepared by MPDEPP-CAG prior to the Bank's identification mission last December 2009, the principal areas where the ministry felt the greatest needs for capacity strengthening included: (i) integration and interconnectivity of the ministry's various information systems; (ii) support to improve staff skills and capacities throughout the public administration in the areas of forecasts, planning, financial management and control; and (iii) institutional support for enhanced coordination and control of the Government Action This proposal seeks to strengthen the organizational and human capacity of the Ministry of Development in the areas of strategic planning, coordination, evaluation, and rapid monitoring of Government's development programs. This will be achieved by (i) enhancing staff skills; (ii) rationalizing its organizational structure and processes; and (iii) developing a rapid monitoring system.
